mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and does not require a threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has been declining for at least 3 months, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a single month, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE rises above 4.5% in a month, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in residential sales (RSAFS) signals a demand shock that is both supply-constrained and demand-pull, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. The interaction between these two series is necessary for the signal to be active.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (INDPRO decline and RSAFS rise) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising above its 12-month moving average and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4.0%, it indicates a strong supply-side economy that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism is most active during periods of strong economic growth.
failure_condition: When the condition (INDPRO > 12mo_MA and UNRATE < 4.0%) is met, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential sales (RSAFS) over the past 3 months signals rising housing demand that boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The signal is always active and does not require a threshold condition.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS has been rising for at least 3 months, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI (CPIAUCSL) rises above 335.0 in a single month, it signals accelerating inflation that triggers a monetary policy tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises above 335.0 in a month, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. The interaction between these two series is necessary for the signal to be active.
failure_condition: The interaction signal (PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise) fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.0% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising above 330.0, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy environment that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days. This mechanism is most active during periods of monetary tightening.
failure_condition: When the condition (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 330.0) is met, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.
